findings.description: storage_encrypted = false means the RDS MySQL instance stores all data, and any snapshots taken from it, unencrypted on disk.

publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance an internet-routable endpoint, exposing MySQL to untrusted networks and leaving only the security group and a static password between attackers and the data.
The master username is hardcoded to the well-known default 'admin', which combined with the public endpoint makes credential guessing and brute force attacks materially easier.

Neither the instance nor its custom parameter group enforces TLS (require_secure_transport), and the PHP client uses plain mysqli_connect, so credentials and query data can cross the network in cleartext to a public endpoint.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced in parameter group
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character-set parameters and omits require_secure_transport = 1, permitting unencrypted client connections to the publicly accessible database.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". This role is attached through the instance profile to an internet-facing PHP web server, so compromise of that host yields account-wide control of S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS (including snapshot exfiltration and privilege escalation paths).

user_data interpolates var.password and the DB master username into a cleartext PHP include file; EC2 user data is readable from the instance metadata service (and stored unencrypted), leaking the database master credentials to anyone with SSRF or shell access on the host.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled; a single SSRF in the exposed PHP application can retrieve the user_data secrets and the over-privileged instance role credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root volume holding the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file may be created unencrypted.

Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, enabling unconstrained outbound traffic that supports data exfiltration and command-and-control from a compromised database tier.
